From: Rebecca Mills <rebecca.mills@tecton.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI - commercial/pricing section (consumption waterfall questions)

Sean,

Thanks for taking our RFI. A few clarifying questions from procurement on the commercial/pricing section — we want the answers to include how you calculate overages (monthly vs. rolling average), whether you offer a committed floor, and how embedding usage is priced relative to generation tokens. Specifically:

- If we commit to a spend or token volume, how do you apply that against mixed workloads (chat + embeddings) across a month?
- Do you support a consumption "waterfall" (commit applies first to generation, then embeddings) or separate buckets?
- How are burst overages charged? Any tiered overage rates or caps?
- Do you offer an annual prepay or true-up cadence and what discounts apply at each commit band?

Attached: our projected per-month split (chat vs embeddings) in Tecton_RFP_questions.xlsx. Examples in numbers would be very helpful.

Appreciate a brief written response we can include in the RFP pack — procurement may follow up with a short call.

Rebecca
Rebecca Mills
Head of Procurement
Tecton Systems

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Mills <rebecca.mills@tecton.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI - commercial/pricing section (consumption waterfall questions)

Rebecca — thanks for the clear list. We've prepared a concise commercial approach and attached a short PDF with diagrams (Redwood_Commercial_Terms_v1.pdf) and a consumption-waterfall-diagram.png that visualizes the flow. High-level summary below; we can do numeric worked examples in a follow-up e-mail.

Summary (high level):
- Commit model: commits can be expressed as tokens/month (preferred) or annual token prepay. Commits create a baseline unit price (Tier A).
- Consumption waterfall: by default we use a single pool with tagging (generation tokens consumed first for baseline commit allocation, embeddings billed against the same pool but with a separate unit multiplier if requested). Alternatively, we can create dedicated buckets for embeddings if you prefer strict separation.
- Overage mechanics: monthly reconciliation. Monthly true-up compares actual consumption to commit. Bursts up to a configurable cushion (typically 5-15% of commit) incur a soft overage at 1.25x baseline; sustained excess beyond the cushion is charged at a graduated overage ladder (e.g., 1.5x then 1.2x as volume bands increase) — designed to encourage moving to a higher commit rather than penalize short spikes.
- True-up cadence & discounts: monthly invoice with quarterly/annual true-up options. Discounts increase with committed annual volumes (three-tier ladder in PDF). Annual prepay gets an additional 3-8% depending on term length.
- Embeddings: priced as a separate logical unit (per-embedding request) or as a token-equivalent with a multiplier; we offer dedicated embedding discounts at scale.
- Special: we offer a rolling 3-month smoothing option for startups with volatile usage; and an SLO-based burst allowance for enterprise customers tied to provisioned dedicated capacity.

I'll have Marissa pull together two concrete invoice examples (low volume and mid-enterprise) and send in-line numbers. In the meantime, link to working doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=redwood-commit-pricing-v1

Best,
Sean
Sr. Sales Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Commercial_Terms_v1.pdf (summary + ladder), consumption-waterfall-diagram.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFI - commercial/pricing section (consumption waterfall questions) — worked example

Rebecca — quick worked example below using the default waterfall (commit applies to generation first, embeddings drawn from same pool but credited at a 0.5 token-equivalent multiplier for billing unless a dedicated bucket is requested). Numbers are illustrative; exact ladder bands in PDF.

Assumptions:
- Monthly commit: 50,000,000 tokens (Commit Tier 2)
- Baseline unit price (Tier 2): $0.0006 / token (generation)
- Embedding unit price: $0.002 / embedding OR 0.5 token-equivalent (we show both views)
- Burst cushion: 10% of commit (5,000,000 tokens) reset monthly (not rolling)
- Overage ladder beyond cushion: first 0–10M tokens at 1.4x baseline, next 10M at 1.15x baseline (softening as volume grows)

Scenario: Actual usage in month
- Generation tokens: 65,000,000
- Embeddings: 10,000 requests (we'll show as both embedding units and token-equivalent)

Step 1 — Allocate commit to generation first:
- Commit covers 50,000,000 generation tokens. Remaining generation demand = 15,000,000 tokens (65M - 50M).

Step 2 — Apply burst cushion:
- Cushion = 5,000,000 tokens. Remaining uncovered generation demand after cushion = 10,000,000 tokens (15M - 5M). Cushion is charged at 1.25x baseline if used.

Step 3 — Overage ladder for uncovered tokens:
- First uncovered 10,000,000 tokens fall into first overage band (1.4x) — charge = 10,000,000 * ($0.0006 * 1.4) = $8,400.
- Cushion charge (if used) = 5,000,000 * ($0.0006 * 1.25) = $3,750.
- Baseline covered tokens charge = 50,000,000 * $0.0006 = $30,000.

Embeddings calculation (two views):
- Per-embedding price = $0.002 * 10,000 = $20,000 (if billed as separate embedding SKU)
OR
- Token-equivalent billing at 0.5 tokens/embedding = 10,000 * 0.5 = 5,000 token-equivalents. If drawn from pool, token-equivalents would consume commit before overage (in our default waterfall embeddings draw from same pool after generation; we gave generation priority).

Total invoice (default waterfall + separate embedding SKU as conservative view):
- Baseline generation: $30,000
- Cushion: $3,750
- Overage ladder: $8,400
- Embeddings (separate SKU): $20,000
- Subtotal: $62,150

Notes and options:
- If you prefer embeddings to unlock discounts, we can count embedding token-equivalents towards tier thresholds. That typically reduces overall price in embedding-heavy workloads.
- Cushion resets monthly (common enterprise pattern); we also offer a 3-month rolling smoothing option if you want to avoid monthly cliffs — that smooths overage charges across quarter.
- Annual prepay at 12 months gives an incremental 5% on top of tier discounts; two-year terms can go to ~8% off baseline.

If you'd like, we can produce an itemized sample invoice CSV that follows your spreadsheet columns and include formulas auditors can validate. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with procurement + finance next week to walk them through this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
